title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: A practical guide to campus places for studying, reflecting, meeting, eating, and recreation—plus the access limits worth checking first.

cards.title: Choose a Study Setup That Fits the Task
cards.subtitle: One building, multiple ways to work
cards.notes: Match the space to the assignment—quiet individual work, technology-supported study, or librarian help—then confirm semester hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Use the library when your work needs more than a chair and an outlet.
cards.evidence_claim: The library provides instructional technologies, varied study spaces, research materials, and assistance from librarians.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to semester hours and posted rules; the published schedule lists no Saturday hours.

cards.title: Use the Chapel for a Quiet Reset
cards.subtitle: Reflection space between scheduled gatherings
cards.notes: Step inside for calm seating or personal reflection, but first look for worship, rehearsals, performances, or other events that may be using the room.
cards.short_summary: The Chapel supports quiet pauses as well as large community programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus describes Christ Chapel as a place for worship, performances, community gatherings, and quiet reflection.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled services, rehearsals, performances, and events may displace quiet use; observe posted access rules.

cards.title: Build a Movement Break Into the Day
cards.subtitle: Recreation and gathering under one roof
cards.notes: Check the current facility schedule, then use Lund for an available recreation option or meet in its student lounge before the next commitment.
cards.short_summary: Lund combines exercise facilities, activity spaces, and a student lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lund Center contains workout and activity facilities, courts, a pool, an ice arena, and a student lounge.
cards.access_notes: Facility schedules, eligibility rules, classes, practices, and events determine which spaces are available.

cards.title: Start an Arboretum Visit Indoors
cards.subtitle: Maps, interpretation, and programmed gatherings
cards.notes: Begin here to orient yourself with maps and interpretive displays, or check the calendar before planning to use the building during a group program.
cards.short_summary: The Arboretum’s main facility adds indoor context to an outdoor visit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Melva Lind Interpretive Center contains maps and interpretive elements and hosts programming, meetings, and special events.
cards.access_notes: The building has limited hours and may be reserved for meetings or events; drop-in availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Walk the Labyrinth Without an Agenda
cards.subtitle: A shaded route for reflection
cards.notes: Use the labyrinth for a slow walking break, stay within maintained areas, and plan the visit for daylight with weather and trail conditions in mind.
cards.short_summary: This defined Arboretum feature offers a deliberate change of pace.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies a shaded labyrinth in the Arboretum as a place to walk, reflect, and contemplate.
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum grounds are available during daylight hours; outdoor conditions and posted policies apply.

cards.title: Bring Collaborative Work to Nobel Hall
cards.subtitle: Whiteboards, lounges, and coffee nearby
cards.notes: Use a student lounge or available study area for solo or group work, and treat laboratories and specialized collections as controlled spaces.
cards.short_summary: Nobel supports informal study alongside its scientific teaching facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus says students study alone or with classmates in Nobel Hall, whose rooms have whiteboards and whose facilities include student lounges.
cards.access_notes: Building access and room availability vary; laboratories, equipment, and research areas may require authorization.

cards.title: Check for Recreational Ice Time
cards.subtitle: A varsity rink with seasonal shared use
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled recreation session between October and March before bringing skates; team practices and events can take priority.
cards.short_summary: The hockey facility also accommodates seasonal recreation beyond varsity use.
cards.evidence_claim: Don Roberts Ice Rink serves varsity hockey and recreational use by students, staff, and the community from October through March.
cards.access_notes: Recreational access is seasonal and schedule-dependent; the source does not establish equipment rental or free admission.

cards.title: Plan a Swim Around the Facility Schedule
cards.subtitle: Recreation shares space with teams and courses
cards.notes: Confirm a recreational period and applicable entry requirements before arriving, since classes, teams, and other scheduled uses share the pool.
cards.short_summary: The pool supports both instruction and designated recreational use.
cards.evidence_claim: Vic Gustafson Pool is used for courses and athletic teams and is also available for recreation by students, staff, faculty, and Gustavus families.
cards.access_notes: Use depends on recreational scheduling and facility requirements; unrestricted public drop-in access is not established.

cards.title: Pair a Nobel Study Session With Food
cards.subtitle: Breakfast, lunch, and coffee inside the science complex
cards.notes: Stop here for a purchased drink or meal while working in Nobel, but check current dining information instead of assuming service hours.
cards.short_summary: The café provides an on-site food option within Nobel Hall’s study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The STEAMery in Nobel Hall offers breakfast and lunch choices, grab-and-go food, smoothies, pastries, and coffee beverages.
cards.access_notes: The source describes the menu but does not establish current hours; food and beverages require purchase.

cards.title: Use the Main-Floor Study and Hangout Areas
cards.subtitle: Resident common space beyond individual rooms
cards.notes: Residents can move between the fireplace conversation area and two larger study-hangout spaces; guests should follow housing access rules.
cards.short_summary: Norelius provides several shared settings within a first-year residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Norelius Hall has pod lounges, a main-level fireplace conversation area called the Pit, and two large study-hangout areas.
cards.access_notes: This is a controlled-access residence hall intended for residents and properly hosted guests, not general public entry.
